likelyCostDrivers: At development rate 60, the accumulator adds 60 per simulation tick against DEVELOPMENT_TICKS_PER_DAY=800, so this 300000-tick workload executes about 22500 development_day passes.

development_day scans buildings for activity/vacancy and housing arrivals and advances projects; sync_residents returns immediately once the resident vector reaches MAX_RESIDENTS=800, so it does not keep scanning residents during this profile’s mature phase.

step_one evaluates growth every 40 ticks, and mature growth may run the bounded progressive frontage scan every 160 ticks (up to 24 roads and 48 sites per evaluation). It also updates resident/delivery schedules every 200 ticks, advances travelers/trains/buses every tick, and advances the district measurement cursor every tick. These are source-grounded candidates, not isolated costs.
sourceInspection.validationCost: restore_json invokes engine.validate twice while rebuilding/canonicalizing a save; step_one does not call engine.validate. The measured ~231ms restore time is small relative to the ~56.7s stepping run, so validation is not the observed stepping hotspot.
sourceInspection.samplingProfilerCheck: Node Inspector sampled only batches 61–150; the resulting self/inclusive rankings and symbol-resolved frame names are included in functionProfile.
sourceInspection.caveat: Sampling is statistical and adds runtime overhead. It identifies sampled CPU work in this steady-maturity window, not a guaranteed optimization or browser frame-time improvement.

limitations: This is a synchronous public-WASM engine workload without rendering, worker scheduling, or browser frame pacing.
Sparse snapshots are outside each timed step batch; their cost is reported separately and is not added to batch durations.
The sampled process RSS and WASM memory are runtime observations, not a device-memory guarantee.
